scenes.line1: What happens when your data changes?
scenes.say: Ever had a source table change columns overnight? Will your ETL or ELT pipeline break, or can it adapt?

scenes.label: Evolution
scenes.sub: Avro and Parquet support schema evolution for adding, removing, or changing columns.
scenes.say: File formats like Avro and Parquet are built for schema evolution. They let you add, drop, or change columns without breaking the pipeline.

rows.b: Set up alerts for schema shifts
Keep old and new model versions
Design for backward and forward use

scenes.say: Here's a solid approach: monitor for schema changes, version your models, and always check for backward and forward compatibility.

scenes.title: Handle new columns
scenes.say: With dbt, you can use alter table commands or versioned models to handle new columns in your data source.

scenes.question: What breaks most pipelines?
scenes.right: Untracked schema changes—like renaming or changing types—can silently break downstream jobs.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: pipelines often break not when you drop unused columns, but when you change column names or types without tracking those changes.
